title: Return Authorization, Restocking and Credit Terms for Ship-To Fulfillment Accounts
content:
**Ship-To Fulfillment Account — returns terms.** Windows, fees and percentages are the level's own, as set in the two returns schedules (windows and returnability; fees and credit). The level is that of the ship-to the goods were shipped to.

### Clauses

1. Returns are authorized per shipped order line by RMA, and the quantity authorized across all open RMAs of a line (the returned quantity of the line: the quantities on its RMA authorizations whose RMA has not been closed without credit) never exceeds the quantity shipped on it.
2. *Retired, no longer in force:* "A customer-reason return (ordered in error or no longer needed) is authorized only when the request is made no later than the level's return window in calendar days after the ship date of the returned line." This clause has been superseded by the current basis.
3. Count calendar days starting the day after the ship date; a request on the last day is authorized.
4. A customer-reason return is declined for an item class among the level's non-returnable item classes, for a special-order item unless the level allows special-order returns and the manufacturer accepts it, and for an opened item unless the level allows opened-item returns.
5. A defective item is returnable within the level's defective return window in calendar days after the ship date; a wrong item shipped or a duplicate shipment is returnable within the level's return window; damage in transit is returnable when reported within the level's damage report period in business days after the delivery date; these Corbett-error returns are accepted for every item class and stock status.
6. Goods must arrive within the level's RMA validity period in calendar days after the RMA date or the RMA line closes without credit as RMA expired; goods found used or damaged by the customer on a customer-reason return close without credit as failed inspection.
7. Return credit is computed on the level's return credit basis: the returned extended amount is the quantity accepted times the invoiced unit price; an opened item is credited at the level's opened item credit percent of that amount.
8. A customer-reason return carries a restocking fee of the level's restocking fee percent of the returned extended amount (the special-order restocking fee percent for an accepted special-order return), rounded half up to the cent and raised to the level's minimum restocking fee when lower, and, when shipped on a Corbett prepaid label, a label fee of the level's return label fee; where the level includes route pickup a route pickup carries no label fee.
9. Where the level waives the restocking fee on Corbett-error returns, a Corbett-error return carries no restocking fee and no label fee and is credited in full regardless of condition.
10. The credit is the credited amount less the restocking fee and the label fee, never below 0.00, issued by credit memo within the level's credit issue period in business days of receipt.

### Counting the days after the ship date

Day 1 is the day after the ship date. *Hypothetical:* with a 45-day period, a line shipped on day 0 has its last day on day 45; a request on day 45 is on the last day.

### Hypothetical credit computation

A customer-reason return of 4 units at an invoiced unit price of 25.00, with a hypothetical restocking fee of 12 percent, a minimum of 8.00 and a label fee of 6.00:

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| Returned extended amount (4 times 25.00) | 100.00 |
| Restocking fee (12 percent, rounded half up to the cent; not below the 8.00 minimum) | 12.00 |
| Label fee (prepaid label used) | 6.00 |
| Credit (100.00 less 12.00 less 6.00, never below 0.00) | 82.00 |

With the same inputs and a hypothetical minimum of 15.00, the restocking fee is raised to 15.00 and the credit is 79.00.

superseded_clauses: A customer-reason return (ordered_in_error or no_longer_needed) is authorized only when the request is made no later than return_window_days calendar days after the ship date of the returned line.
